---
title: "The synthetic authenticity benchmark"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 96, out.width = "100%")
```

**Experimental.** `authenticity_benchmark()` compares several language models
on Overlap, Structure and Behaviour, and puts them in one table with a single
score per model. The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about
them. It does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.

## A first benchmark

Like the Behaviour functions, `authenticity_benchmark()` takes raw answers and
an item table and does the keying itself. Here are two traits, Honesty-Humility
and Conscientiousness (80 items), for Canada, with three attempts per model:

```{r}
library(synthcheck)

items <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait %in% c("H", "C"), ]
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 3, ]
synthetic <- as_synthetic_list(ca, items = items$item)
```

```{r}
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, items, n_splits = 10, n_floor = 10)
bm
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
gg_benchmark(bm)
```

## Reading the anchored values

Every column is rescaled between two anchors:

- **Floor (0):** A dumb generator that draws each item column on its own from
  the real data. It keeps every item's distribution but breaks people apart.
- **Ceiling (100):** A second, separate sample of real people, scored against
  the first with the same index.

So 100 means "as close to real people as other real people are", and 0 means
"no better than shuffled columns". Values below 0 mean the model is further
from real people than shuffled real answers: Its respondents bunch into fewer
score deciles (Overlap), its items correlate more than real ones (Structure),
or its answers are tidier than real people's (Behaviour). Tables show the
values as they are, and `gg_benchmark()` colours them from red (-100 or lower)
through pale (0) to blue (100).

```{r}
bm$anchors
```

`n_floor` and `n_splits` set how many shuffled draws and real splits are
averaged (20 by default). With `ceiling_n = "attempt"` (the default), the
ceiling samples are the size of a typical synthetic attempt, so the
sampling noise is comparable. `ceiling_n = "half"` uses the two halves of the
real data.

## Choosing the score

The default score is the **weakest** column, named in `weakest`: A model is
only as authentic as its weakest side. You can change it:

```{r}
bm_mean <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, items, score = "mean",
                                  weights = c(overlap = 1, structure = 1, behaviour = 2),
                                  n_splits = 10, n_floor = 10)
bm_mean$table[, c("model", "score", "overlap", "structure", "behaviour")]
```

`score = "geometric"` takes the geometric mean of the clamped values, and a
function of `overlap`, `structure` and `behaviour` gives your own score.

## The plain-language summary

```{r}
summarise_benchmark(bm)
```

The text follows fixed rules and states only values in the table, so the
same benchmark always gives the same summary.

## The pieces behind the table

```{r}
names(bm)
bm$attempts
```

`bm$behaviour` is the full `synthetic_behaviour()` result, so the behaviour
strip comes for free:

```{r, fig.height = 5}
gg_behaviour(bm$behaviour)
```

## Settings that change the target

- `clean_real = TRUE`: Compare against real respondents after careless ones
  are removed (see [Behaviour](behaviour.html)). The flags are in
  `bm$careless`.
- `fit_scales`: The scales used for person fit. `character(0)` skips person
  fit, which makes the benchmark much faster while you explore.
- `cor = "polychoric"`: Polychoric correlations for Structure (needs polycor,
  slow on many items).

## All 240 items

The full benchmark, with person fit on all six traits, takes several minutes:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada", ]
bm_all <- authenticity_benchmark(as_synthetic_list(ca), real, hexaco_items)
gg_benchmark(bm_all)
```
